title: Sectoral AI Governance Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Sectoral AI Governance Act of 2026 establishes specific regulatory frameworks for the use of artificial intelligence across key sectors such as healthcare, finance, and national security, requiring compliance with sector‑specific standards. The law aims to balance innovation with public safety by mandating transparency, risk assessments, and oversight for AI applications within each industry.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This act aims to prevent companies from exploiting AI services to charge excessively high prices and manipulate wages. It establishes regulations and penalties to ensure fair pricing and fair labor practices in the AI industry.

title: American AI Security Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The American AI Security Act is a proposed U.S. law that aims to regulate the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence systems so they do not pose significant risks to national security or public safety. It establishes oversight requirements, risk assessment protocols, and accountability measures for AI developers and operators while encouraging innovation and responsible AI practices.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that Congress must refuse to provide any additional funds or exceptional regulatory support to companies or financial institutions facing insolvency or financial collapse due to exposures to acute stress within the artificial intelligence market and must provide support to all harmed Americans instead.
action: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House says Congress should not give extra money or special regulatory help to companies or banks that are on the brink of collapse because of problems in the artificial‑intelligence market. Instead, the House urges Congress to direct assistance toward all Americans who have been harmed.

title: VET Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The VET Artificial Intelligence Act provides guidelines for how AI tools can be integrated into vocational education and training settings, ensuring that their use is ethical, transparent, and aligned with industry needs. It aims to protect students, promote fair access to AI resources, and establish accountability for educators and employers who deploy these technologies.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 requires that medical diagnosis, treatment, and patient care be performed exclusively by licensed human doctors, not by artificial intelligence systems. It aims to protect patients by ensuring that AI can only serve as a tool to assist doctors, not replace their professional judgment or decision‑making.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 requires companies to assess and document the impact of AI and automated decision‑making systems, especially those used in hiring, lending, or law enforcement. It sets standards for transparency, auditing, and reporting to ensure algorithms do not produce unfair or discriminatory outcomes.

title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Securing Elections From AI Deception Act is aimed at protecting the integrity of elections by limiting the use of AI tools that can create misleading or false political content. It sets rules for detecting, labeling, and regulating AI‑generated messages so voters can better identify trustworthy information.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 establishes federal guidelines and oversight to ensure that AI systems are developed, tested, and deployed with high reliability, safety, and transparency. It provides funding, sets research standards, and requires reporting and risk assessments to protect public trust in AI technologies.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 aims to establish clear guidelines for the use of artificial intelligence within the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs. It requires the VA to disclose how AI systems make decisions, ensuring accountability and protecting veterans' privacy.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act is a proposed law aimed at ensuring that artificial intelligence systems used by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs to process disability and benefits claims are fair, transparent, and reliable. It seeks to establish clear guidelines and oversight mechanisms so that veterans can trust the decisions made by automated tools, and to hold the VA accountable if those tools produce errors or bias.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is a proposed law aimed at safeguarding consumers from misleading or deceptive uses of artificial intelligence. The Act seeks to enforce transparency, accurate labeling, and accountability for AI systems that could misinform or manipulate consumers.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act aims to establish comprehensive standards for AI systems to ensure they are secure and reliable before deployment. The legislation requires organizations to conduct rigorous security assessments, implement robust safeguards, and adhere to ongoing monitoring to protect against malicious use and unintended harm.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act establishes a new task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to coordinate national efforts for protecting artificial intelligence systems from cyber threats. It outlines the task force’s responsibilities, funding, and collaboration with private sector partners to develop best‑practice guidelines and rapid response protocols.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 is designed to establish guidelines and regulations for managing and mitigating the risks associated with AI systems. It aims to promote safety, accountability, and transparency in the development, deployment, and use of AI technologies to protect public interests.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 establishes a national framework for the safe and responsible deployment of AI-enabled physical systems, such as robots, autonomous vehicles, and drones. It creates coordination mechanisms and oversight requirements to ensure these technologies meet safety standards, protect public interests, and promote transparent collaboration among developers, regulators, and users.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is a proposed law that aims to safeguard the integrity of elections by regulating the use of artificial intelligence in political campaigns. It seeks to prevent deceptive AI‑generated content from influencing voters and to ensure transparency and accountability when AI is employed in election-related communications.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act proposes a framework to track and regulate AI systems that can autonomously modify their own code or behavior. It requires developers to report updates, maintain transparency, and establishes oversight to prevent unintended or harmful outcomes.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act aims to prevent autonomous AI systems from acting without human oversight, ensuring that they operate safely and responsibly. It proposes new regulations and oversight mechanisms to curb potentially dangerous or unregulated AI behavior.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act would pause the construction or operation of new AI data centers for a specified period, aiming to address concerns about environmental impact, energy consumption, and societal effects. By temporarily halting the expansion of these facilities, the act seeks to encourage more sustainable practices and give policymakers time to develop longer‑term regulations for the AI industry.
